thread:
alex: Ok team — follow-up on the 'stitchless fission' idea. Goal is safer long-term modularization with minimal runtime stitching. Quick sanity-check: what are the non-negotiables we need to preserve during an extract?

mica: Non-negotiables: end-to-end trace continuity, per-tenant rate limits, and no client-facing latency regressions >15%. Also want feature parity tests. :white_check_mark:

ravi: DB concern — some of the hot paths do cross multiple tables in the monolith transaction. Do we do a dual-write strategy or build a read-side copy first? Dual-write complicates rollback.

sam: +1 on read-side copy first. Phase 1: extract read-only handler behind a facade, route a shadow copy of traffic to new service for perf/compat checks. Phase 2: cutover writes when we have stable sync and can tolerate eventual consistency.

jules: main worry is cross-service transactions (billing, quotas). We should define compensation flows and idempotency up front. Also we need an explicit fallback if the new service returns 5xx or times out — fallback to monolith call for N seconds while we roll back.

alex: Agreed. Canary plan sketch: 1) 0% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over days. Automated health gates: error-rate >0.5% OR 95th latency +20% triggers rollback. We'll automate rollback via the rollout controller.

mica: Observability checklist: a) preserve trace_id header across calls, b) emit "migration.phase" tag on traces, c) metric for cache hit ratio and kv-latency for extracted path. Also perf budget for p95.

ravi: For data migration, propose this sequence: snapshot -> backfill -> CDC tailing -> validation window -> cutover. Need clear validation queries. I can own backfill scripts but need schema contract docs.

sam: Contract tests between monolith and extracted service must be runnable in CI. Minimal example: request/response shape + side-effects smoke. We should add a fast contract runner to the PR checks.

jules: Staffing ask: extraction window will need 1x owner + 1x infra on-call for first 72 hours. Cost: estimate 2-3 engineer-weeks per extraction slice + infra egress. We should prioritize slices with smallest state & highest cohesion first.

alex: Practical guardrails: - max 3 concurrent extractions - define "slice" as cross-functional capability with <2 DB hotspots - each slice must have a rollback playbook and runbook entry.

mica: We also need an API deprecation cadence: keep compat shim for 14 days after 100% traffic, then flip feature flag off. Communicate to SDK teams.

ravi: Example compatibility shim config snippet (can be in router):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/enrich",
  "fallback": "monolith-enrich",
  "timeout_ms": 400,
  "max_retries": 1
}
```

sam: Nice. Add a rate-penalty when in canary to reduce the blast radius for noisy tenants. Also add per-tenant kill-switch.

jules: On tech-debt paydown: capture required refactors as discrete tickets with estimated rollback cost. Start with the enrichment and session surfaces since they have clear boundaries.

ops-bot: CI:canary-pipeline triggered by alex - canary-deploy/1719954321 started. Status: queued.

alex: Next actions: 1) mica + ravi to draft migration spike and validation queries by EOW, 2) sam to add contract-runner PR template, 3) jules to size staffing and cost and propose prioritized slice list. I'll schedule a 30m sync next Tue. If no objections I'll mark this as kickoff.

mica: Ack — I'll drop the validation SQL and trace tag list into the spike doc.

ravi: I'll stub the backfill plan and the schema contract doc.

sam: I'll prototype the contract-runner and add it to the QA pipeline.

jules: I'll send prioritized slice list + on-call roster.

alex: Sweet. Minimal timeline expectation: spikes this week, first extraction spike next sprint. Keeping the surface minimal and stitchless where possible. :rocket:
